Ep. 1: director Daisuke Nishio, animation supervisor Masayuki Uchiyama, aired 26 Apr 1989. Ep. 2: director Osamu Kasai, animation supervisor Katsumi Aoshima, aired 3 May 1989. Ep. 2's anime-only verdict: 'nothing notable, aside from general padding'. Both compress into Kai ep. 1.
Ep. 2's working title was 'Father Son Goku's Past'; the auctioned script lists Piccolo in the cast as Ma Junior.
Gohan is born 18 May, Age 757; Raditz arrives 28 November, Age 761 — so the boy is four.
No parent of Goku's is named anywhere in episode 2 — only "our father and mother". Bardock and Gine are named elsewhere in the franchise and not here (CC 00:20:50).

facts.statement: Ep. 3, at home (14:56–15:08): Chi-Chi assumes the two of them are having fun at Roshi's, then remembers the cram-school homework is only half done, and sighs. She is not worried yet.

Ep. 4, at home (22:43–23:17): she is humming, holding a returned test paper, pleased that eight hours of study a day paid off, and saying she wishes the two of them would come home so she could show it to Goku.
In the anime Piccolo arrives hovering above Kame House; in the manga he had been hidden around the corner of it, listening.
The Special Beam Cannon reads 1,330 in ep. 4 (spoken, 17:13) and 1,480 for the final shot in ep. 5 (spoken, 10:26). Both are spoken; the 1,485 in the episode page is wrong (R-20).
Dub dialogue for the rules scene: Goku says Chi-Chi is overprotective, makes Gohan study all the time, and calls martial arts a waste of energy.
Dub monologue, ep. 5: 'Goku should've been home by now… It's not good for Gohan to be away from his studies this long… He deserves to have a little fun once in a while.'

The mountain thread: ep. 3 the half-done homework · ep. 4 the returned test and the eight hours · ep. 5 the Ox-King arriving with presents · ep. 6 the phone call that reaches an answering machine. She is at home in all four and knows nothing yet.

**The telling does not happen in ep. 6.** Roshi orders Krillin to go, Bulma says the mother will kill him, and the phone gets the Kame House answering machine (14:48–15:31). **It does not happen in ep. 7 either** — Krillin gets as far as her gate, bottles it, and lies (C120).

Daizenshuu 7 places Raditz's arrival at 12 October, Age 761; the 23rd Budōkai on 7 May 756; Gohan's birth in May 757; Vegeta and Nappa on 3 November 762. Kanzenshuu notes the dates were assigned backwards from later anchors.
The Great Ape multiplies a Saiyan's base power by ten, and needs the tail and the full moon.

A secondary episode comparison reports that the Makankōsappō reading is anime-only. The local Japanese episode-5 caption says 1,480; the former alternative secondary figure is withdrawn (C062, R-20). The manga comparison remains separately sourced.

facts.statement: FORM: EPISODE is the default for new chapters, with anime grammar and the form-aware 4,400–6,600 word band. Chapters One and Two are accepted legacy scenes pending episode-form rebuild. Camera movement does not confer canon-character interiority.

facts.statement: A fight is clear in geography, participants, actions, stakes and consequences. Flight, named techniques, multiple supernatural actions and sourced or authored readings are allowed. Damage follows feats, attack, aim and conditions, not a fixed formula (WRITING §§11,16).
facts.source: author ruling — fights and the supernatural are the weakest writing

facts.statement: Write supernatural action directly and coherently: cause, movement, effect, consequence. Do not compare it to ordinary furniture, flag it as impossible or report what could not be seen. Multiple supernatural actions and visible ordinary ki are allowed; no early god ki (WRITING §12).
facts.source: author ruling — fights and the supernatural are the weakest writing

facts.statement: CRAFT.md has three authored specimens: controlled spar, hillside blast and flight/technique practice. They are exercises, not canonical beats.
facts.source: author ruling — fights and the supernatural are the weakest writing

facts.statement: **Once a character is named on the page, the narration calls them by that name.** No epithets for named characters — not 'the taller boy', not 'the small one', not 'the demon', not 'the woman with blue hair'. **Three legal exceptions only:** before the name is known (once), for a character who is never named (declared as furniture), and inside dialogue. **Gated by `check_names`.**
facts.source: author ruling — epithets read as withholding

facts.topic: craft — the crib, and the clarity law
facts.statement: **A fight must be followable in one pass** (`WRITING §11 law 0`): every paragraph answers *where are they · who is acting · what changed*. **One action per sentence; no pronoun with two possible owners.** Effect-only prose is a mood, not a sequence. **Every specimen carries a plain-words crib first** — numbered, adjective-free — because if the crib is unclear the prose is broken, not the reader.
facts.source: author ruling — the fight could not be followed

facts.topic: craft — no riddles in invented material
facts.statement: Invented material must be plain and understandable without prior scenes. Characters do not speak in aphorisms or announce facts already shown: the authority orders and the learner acts. Context and action make the stake clear; every craft specimen begins with WHAT THIS IS and a plain-words crib.
facts.source: author ruling — the invented prose reads as a riddle

facts.statement: **The impossible runs on flow** (`WRITING §15`). **Never tell the reader they could not see it** — *no 'nobody saw', no 'blink of an eye'*; write the displacement and let the ground report it. **Never compare the impossible to something ordinary** — no doors, pages, bowls, fists. **Never stop to say it is strange** — the reader knows. Shape: **cause you can point at → event → consequence left in the world**, no gaps. **And a character may not announce what the scene already shows:** no *'he has a tail'* — let the one with authority give the order and the boy act.
facts.source: author ruling — the supernatural comparisons and the announcements read wrong

facts.statement: A fight declares its participants, condition, relevant demonstrated capabilities, attack and environment. Damage follows the scene and feats, not a numerical battle-power conversion. Bodies are not categorically small-damage and large feats need not always require a long charge (WRITING §16).

facts.statement: User-authored standing: Goshin is never less capable than Gohan where both are compared. This is not a deduction from early scouter readings or a claim that Gohan stops growing. Temporary injury, exhaustion, suppression or a tactical loss can affect performance without erasing capability.
facts.source: author ruling — the OC is not the lesser brother

facts.topic: OC — the Talent at the training year
facts.statement: Goshin demonstrates the Talent in the training year: flight, technique use, rapid learning and retained skill. His tail remains a vulnerability unless defended or resistance is trained; a single observation is not automatic immunity. Both children can grow during survival and formal training.
facts.source: author ruling — the retention law at work in the year

facts.statement: The Kame House reading of ~400 is a snapshot, not a permanent level or minimum. Goshin grows as a Saiyan/Earthling hybrid through training, experience, recovery and adaptation. Growth has no invented fixed rate; a lower temporary reading does not erase retained skills.
facts.source: author ruling — the OC grows; the 400 was a reading, not a level

facts.statement: The former automatic ceiling below Nappa, hard prohibition on overtaking printed canon fighters, mandatory canon deaths and fixed plot order are WITHDRAWN. The altered story follows the consequences of its actual divergence, while retaining the user’s Goshin/Gohan standing rule.
